Tensormesh is offering **$100 in free GPU credits** to new users as part of their beta launch. This promotional offer allows you to test their AI inference optimization platform at no initial cost.[1][2][3]

### How to Claim the Credits

You can claim your $100 in free GPU credits by signing up on the Tensormesh website at ** The offer is available to new users who want to try their platform and see how much they can save on their AI infrastructure costs.[2][3][1]

Tensormesh is an AI inference platform that uses advanced KV caching techniques to reduce inference costs by up to 10 times. ## Tensormesh: Free GPU Credits Offer

**Tensormesh is offering $100 in free GPU credits** to new users who sign up for their beta platform. This promotional offer allows developers and teams to test the platform's AI inference optimization technology at no upfront cost.[1][2][3]

### How to Claim the Credits

To claim your $100 in free GPU credits, visit **tensormesh.ai** and sign up for the beta program. The credits can be applied to GPU compute costs on the platform, allowing you to experiment with the service and measure the actual savings on your own workloads.[2][4][1]

### What Tensormesh Does

Tensormesh is an AI inference optimization platform that uses advanced KV (Key-Value) cache techniques to reduce GPU costs by up to 10 times. The platform intelligently routes GPU workloads and implements CPU offloading for KV cache storage, making inference significantly cheaper and faster. The company raised $4.5 million in seed funding and is based on the open-source LMCache utility maintained by co-founder Yihua Cheng.[4][5][6]

### Key Features

The platform supports rapid model deployment—deploying an open-source LLM takes under 30 seconds. Users can select their cloud provider and GPU type (including H200), choose models from Tensormesh's library or connect directly from HuggingFace, and enable KV cache optimization with one click. The beta includes support for various LLM frameworks and is continuously adding features like serverless support.[4]

### Ideal Use Cases

Tensormesh is particularly effective for workloads with repeated context, such as chatbots and retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) systems, where KV cache persistence can deliver the most significant cost savings. The platform offers an OpenAI-compatible API for easy integration without requiring code changes to existing applications.[7][4]
